content.comment_body: Hello, I've developed a program that connects pushbuttons using [product_name], but I'm unable to get [product_name] to control the pushbuttons via the web interface. For example, I tried to switch on input 20 by enabling the I block and selecting 20, but I can't make it writable. I also tried using the device's internal relay M20, which can be made writable, but it still doesn't work. I'm not sure what I'm missing. Reading analog values and setpoints works fine. Additionally, I can only use Microsoft Edge to view or display the program on the web editor. When I hover over the button, a 'No Entry' symbol appears. I noticed that when assigning tags in [product_name], I now see 'Variable 1', which is linked to input 20, but I still can't modify the button on the webpage.

Hello [user_name], Writing to input 20 isn't possible; that's why the writable checkbox is hidden. You can read the status of input 20 without any issue. To switch input 20, you need to have a physical sensor or digital input connected. Hope this helps.

Inputs like 20 can't be set via [product_name]; only their status can be read. This rule also applies to markers if their control is assigned. If you want to operate markers from [product_name], their input should not be connected in the device's program. Regards, [user_name], (translated by Google)
A tip: use a network input and select V memory—it's an effective way to test things. :)
This approach also helps conserve markers and keeps the configuration more organized.
Thanks! I've written the code in ladder logic; I’ll see how I can adapt it.

Hello [user_name], With the new year coming, thank you for your advice! I wasn't aware of this limitation and spent hours troubleshooting. My program is written in ladder logic, so I need to find a way to control this via [product_name]. Thanks again, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion reveals a limitation in the web interface setup for pushbutton control: digital inputs, such as input 20, can only have their statuses read remotely—they cannot be set or written from the web interface through [product_name]. This constraint leads to user confusion and extended troubleshooting, as the system does not make I/O restrictions obvious within the editor, causing a disconnect between user expectations and actual functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to remotely control and make digital inputs writable through the web interface. They are looking for a clearer and more guided setup that explicitly indicates which elements are interactive and writable.
